text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Palestinian Authority: Hebron deal includes final status talks schedule.
- General Security Service advised Prime Minister Netanyahu to remove Hebron settlers.
- Government rips Histadrut labour federation, workers over strike.
- Chief of Staff Shahak: War with Syria not imminent.
- End of the line for Cairo bus line.
HAARETZ
- Defence Minister Mordechai and Palestinian President Arafat to meet in attempt to solve disputes in Hebron deal.
- Electric company, water company, sea ports workers to take disruptive steps today.
- Treasury responds to coalition member demands amounting to some billion shekels.
- Russian proposal to Israel Aircraft Industries to cooperate in upgrading Mig-21 planes.
- Palestinians: 'Israel conceded on buffer zones', Netanyahu's office denies.
- Israel ambassador to U.S.: Netanyahu and Clinton to meet in January in Washington.
- 1997 expected inflation 10.2 percent.
MAARIV
- Rejection front on the right against Hebron deal; safety net for government on left.
- Economic disruptions to sharpen.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Mordechai and Arafat expected to meet today.
- Israel to discuss proposal to change Jerusalem to capital of three religions. Foreign Minister Levy: we'll discuss it after we finish Hebron negotiations.
- Finance Minister Meridor threatens: we'll sue Histadrut if it strikes tomorrow.
